doc.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013

title: Learning phrasing and storytelling from Joe Williams
summary: Touring with Joe Williams and Basie taught Gardner phrasing, timing, lyrics and blues singing.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Joe Williams. Oh man. It was such a — I felt like I was in school the entire time when we got the chance to perform with Joe Williams along with the Basie band. We did several tours with him. And wow. His sense of phrasing and timing, and the way that he just treats a tune was impeccable. Every note and every lyric that he sang was perfectly placed. Almost like he was reading from a page. And he was able to take an audience and just put the audience right in his hand, and the whole audience is just like that — just waiting. He had total command of the audience. There was one tune that Shirley Horn made famous, called “Here’s to Life,” man. And Joe Williams did it. And Joe just tore it up, really did such a beautiful job with it. And the audience was just — you could hear a pin drop. And so I definitely learned to take my time by listening to him. I was able to learn the meaning of the tune through him, because the way that he sang it was like he was telling you a story you know. So oh that’s what the tune’s about. And a lot of times instrumentalists just get into the notes. Just when you learn tunes, just learn notes. You don’t learn the lyrics of the tune and find out what the tune is about you know. And upon hearing Joe sing these tunes I’m learning what the tune is about — not in the manner that he’s singing it to me but more like he’s telling a story. But then we haven’t even talked about the blues yet. That’s a whole nother thing. This was just a whole graduate mini- course on how to sing the blues. If you need any help with doing that, go to Joe Williams.
